Race condition protection pattern in AnimalLembretes component

Sequential token mechanism prevents stale async operation results

The AnimalLembretes.svelte component implements a robust race condition prevention pattern for handling asynchronous reminder loading operations. When `loadReminders()` is called, it increments a sequence counter and captures the current value as `myToken`. Throughout the async operation, before updating any state (loading status, failure state, or data), the code verifies that `myToken === loadSeq`. This ensures that if a newer request was initiated while an older one was still pending, the stale response is discarded. Additionally, the component uses an `actioning` object keyed by reminder ID to prevent concurrent action submissions on the same reminder, disabling buttons during in-flight operations.

- Component uses `loadSeq` counter incremented on each `loadReminders()` call
- Each async operation captures `myToken = ++loadSeq` at invocation time
- Results are only applied if `myToken === loadSeq`, discarding stale responses
- Pattern is consistently applied across multiple state updates: loading, loadFailed, and data assignments
- Component also uses `actioning` object to track per-reminder action states, preventing duplicate submissions

WhatsApp Message Template Resolution Priority in waAction

Template selection follows explicit priority chain: message override → environment variable templates → hardcoded fallback

The agent investigated how WhatsApp message templates are resolved in the waAction endpoint. The codebase implements a sophisticated template selection system that prioritizes explicit message overrides from callers, then falls back to environment-variable-configured templates keyed by name (e.g., 'clicou', 'abriu'), then to a default template, and finally to hardcoded content. This design maintains backward compatibility while allowing flexible template configuration. The system also implements intelligent bucketing to deduplicate requests with the same template across a time window, while keeping custom messages in separate buckets to preserve their uniqueness.

- waAction.js implements a 4-tier template selection priority for WhatsApp messages

- Priority 2: HUB_WA_TEMPLATE_<TEMPLATE> environment variables via input.template parameter
- Priority 3: HUB_WA_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE environment variable (fallback)
- Priority 4: Hardcoded template (last resort to prevent dispatch without body)
- Template bucketing system groups messages by (action, lead, bucket_template) for stable deduplication windows
- Invalid templates or missing environment variables collapse to '_default' bucket
- Custom messages via input.message override get their own '_message_override' bucket
- hubLateClient.js sends template_corpo (not message_template) to the API

COVISA Selenium: ChromeDriver 147 vs Chrome 149 (apontar env p/ cache)

SessionNotCreatedException ao subir o session server

On 2026-06-11, the COVISA skill's session-start failed with SessionNotCreatedException because Chrome had auto-updated to version 149.0.7827.102 while the system's default ChromeDriver remained at version 147. The selenium_session_server.py uses CHROMEDRIVER_BIN environment variable which pointed to /usr/local/bin/chromedriver. Rather than modifying system binaries, the fix was to set HYPER_COVISA_CHROMEDRIVER to point to the correct cached driver version that Selenium Manager had already downloaded on 2026-06-05 at ~/.cache/selenium/chromedriver/linux64/149.0.7827.53/chromedriver-linux64/chromedriver. Since ChromeDriver matches by major version, 149.0.7827.53 is compatible with Chrome 149.0.7827.102. This resolves a recurring issue that appears each time Chrome updates to a new major version. Future prevention: when Chrome updates to a new major version, check ~/.cache/selenium for the corresponding driver and export HYPER_COVISA_CHROMEDRIVER accordingly, or update /usr/local/bin/chromedriver.

- Fix: export HYPER_COVISA_CHROMEDRIVER=~/.cache/selenium/chromedriver/linux64/149.0.7827.53/chromedriver-linux64/chromedriver
- ChromeDriver matches by major version (149.x supports Chrome 149.x)
- Selenium Manager had already cached the correct driver version on 2026-06-05

Comprehensive Frontend Security Audit: XSS and CSRF Posture

Raio-X G audit of 86k-line frontend (Svelte, EJS, public/js) confirms strong XSS/CSRF defenses with 3 ALTA/MEDIA findings and 2 BAIXA code-smell items

A comprehensive security audit of the LATE frontend across three architectural layers (Svelte component framework, EJS server-side templates, and vanilla public JavaScript) confirms a well-defended posture against XSS and CSRF attacks. The codebase demonstrates consistent disciplined patterns: Svelte avoids dangerous directives entirely, all state-changing operations use CSRF-protected fetch wrappers with token rotation, and both EJS and public/js follow strict output encoding rules. The audit identified five findings, none of which represent immediately exploitable vulnerabilities. The single ALTA finding (EJS-G-01) is a supply-chain and CSP-enforcement risk from an unvetted external CDN dependency. The two MEDIA findings (EJS-G-02, EJS-G-03) are latent XSS vectors that are currently mitigated by read-only field status and numeric-only data sources, but represent fragile defenses that violate the project's hard anti-XSS rules and should be hardened before pattern reuse. The two BAIXA findings are code-smell and optional standardization improvements. The audit explicitly documented 13 categories of clean code (zero {@ html}, consistent CSRF, safe innerHTML escaping, protected RBAC, no eval, safe data attributes, etc.) to prevent re-audit drift.

Ao iniciar o session-start da skill COVISA em 11/jun, o Chrome falhou com SessionNotCreatedException: "This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 147 / Current browser version is 149.0.7827.102". O Chrome auto-atualizou para 149 mas /usr/local/bin/chromedriver (usado por default pelo selenium_session_server.py via CHROMEDRIVER_BIN) ainda era 147. É o mesmo crash (stack trace "unknown") que já aparecia no covisa-session.log antigo — problema recorrente a cada bump do Chrome. Fix sem mexer no binário do sistema: setar a env HYPER_COVISA_CHROMEDRIVER apontando para o driver 149 que o Selenium Manager já tinha baixado em ~/.cache/selenium/chromedriver/linux64/149.0.7827.53/chromedriver-linux64/chromedriver (baixado 05/jun). ChromeDriver casa por major version, então 149.0.7827.53 serve para Chrome 149.0.7827.102. Após relançar com a env, o driver subiu e o HTTPServer respondeu na 18888. Para o futuro: quando o Chrome subir de major, conferir ~/.cache/selenium para o driver correspondente e exportar HYPER_COVISA_CHROMEDRIVER (ou atualizar /usr/local/bin/chromedriver).

Confirmado: ao maximizar (Win+seta / F11), o branco sumiu. Regra geral: branco só direita/baixo em tela grande = janela não maximizada (ou overscan da TV se for nas 4 bordas), NÃO mexer no código antes de confirmar maximizando.</narrative>

CAUSA RAIZ: Alpine 3.x processa a diretiva x-model no elemento <select> ANTES de o x-for interno renderizar as <option>s. O efeito reativo que executa `el.value = modelValue` (ex: 'Gato') nao encontra option correspondente naquele momento e silencia. Como pet.species nao muda depois (ja estava com o valor correto do banco), o efeito nunca re-executa. O usuario consegue SELECIONAR valores (porque o browser atualiza select.value antes do handler Alpine) e salvar (save funcionava), mas ao recarregar o ciclo se repete - sempre em branco.

DIAGNOSTICO: dados estavam no banco: species='Gato', sex='Femea', neutered='Nao', vaccinated='Sim', dewormed='Sim'. O save nunca falhou.

FIX: Substituir x-for Alpine dentro dos <select>s por options renderizadas estaticamente pelo EJS no servidor. Com isso as <option>s existem no DOM quando Alpine inicializa, e x-model encontra a option correspondente na primeira execucao do efeito.

Depois de mover uma key AIza válida para ~/.env/.gemini, o bridge AINDA falhava na Live API com "API Key not found", mesmo a key tendo dado setupComplete num teste WS isolado. Causa raiz: ~/.bashrc:128 exporta `GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSyDiHLjs..."` (uma SEGUNDA key AIza, diferente, e INVÁLIDA na Live API — close 1007). O Node `--env-file` NÃO sobrescreve variáveis já presentes no ambiente do processo (comportamento documentado: env existente tem precedência sobre o arquivo). Como o shell do Bash carrega o .bashrc, o processo do bridge herdava a key inválida do .bashrc e ignorava a key boa do .gemini. Confirmado medindo sha256 das duas (diferentes) e testando cada uma na Live API: a do .bashrc falha (1007), a do .gemini (do log) dá setupComplete. Fix: bridge.js agora lê ~/.env/.gemini diretamente via fs e SOBRESCREVE process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY com PRECEDENCIA, logando o prefixo carregado — não depende mais de --env-file nem do ambiente. Há portanto 2 keys AIza vazadas em texto puro na frota: uma em claude-mem-2026-05-12.log (válida, já redigida+movida) e outra em ~/.bashrc:128 (inválida na Live, possivelmente usada por claude-mem; NÃO mexida — alertado ao usuário).</narrative>

Ao explorar a comunidade GitHub/Asterisk sobre a integração tradutor de voz, encontramos a causa-raiz OFICIAL do nosso bug do slin16 (que tínhamos resolvido empiricamente com workaround). O protocolo AudioSocket usa o tipo de frame 0x10 = SLIN 8 kHz FIXO. Sample rates maiores (slin12/16/24/32/44/48/96/192) exigem os tipos de frame 0x11-0x18, adicionados pelo PR #1492 do Asterisk (res_audiosocket: add message types for all slin sample rates, por SvenKube) — disponível só em versões recentes (Asterisk 23+). Há thread na comunidade Asterisk relatando exatamente nosso sintoma: 'AudioSocket defaulting to 8kHz despite slin16 argument in Asterisk 23' — backend recebe/envia tipo 0x10 (320 bytes/8kHz) em vez de 0x12 (640 bytes/16kHz), causando pitch errado. CONCLUSÃO: nosso Asterisk 20.6 NÃO tem os tipos 0x11-0x18, por isso slin16 falhava na escrita (tratado como 8kHz) — o 'grunido'. O workaround que adotamos (externalMedia format=slin 8kHz, resample na borda) é a solução CORRETA para Asterisk 20.6. MELHORIA FUTURA: ao atualizar para Asterisk 23+ (com PR #1492), dá pra usar slin16 nativo (tipo 0x12) e eliminar o downsample 24→8 (melhora a qualidade, tira o aliasing residual). Projetos da comunidade para aprender/comparar: NPCL-Asterisk-ARI-Assistant (Gemini 2.5 + ARI + Live API), hkjarral/AVA-AI-Voice-Agent (AudioSocket+RTP dual transport), pc-m/transcript-demo (externalMedia transcrição). Issues Gemini Live relevantes ao nosso VAD/audioStreamEnd: respostas vazias (livekit/agents #4066), cutoff prematuro com turnComplete (googleapis/js-genai #707), short-utterance não dispara resposta em telefonia.</narrative>
